chunks: And it is also narrated from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he
said: 'Whatever enters the qafeez, it follows the same ruling as wheat, barley, dates, and raisins.'
He said: 'So inform me, may I be sacrificed for you — is there zakat on rice and what resembles it from the grains, chickpeas, and lentils?'
So he (peace be upon him) wrote in response: 'They were right — zakat is on every thing that is measured (by volume).'

key_terms.الْقَفِيزُ: Qafeez — a classical dry measure container (approximately 528 litres), used as the standard unit for calculating zakat on grains
key_terms.زَكَاةٌ: Zakat — obligatory almsgiving/tax on agricultural produce; one of the five pillars
key_terms.فَوَقَّعَ: He wrote/signed (tawqi') — the Imam's written response, a characteristic communication method
key_terms.كِيلَ: Measured (by volume) — the ruling criterion: zakat applies to anything that can be measured volumetrically

ai.seo_question: Is zakat obligatory on rice, chickpeas, and lentils according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) is asked about the application of zakat to grains beyond the traditionally enumerated four: wheat, barley, dates, and raisins. His written response (tawqi') establishes that the general principle is measurement by volume — anything measured by the qafeez (a standard dry measure of roughly 528 litres) is subject to zakat, just as the four canonical items are. The questioner's inquiry about rice, chickpeas, and lentils receives confirmation that zakat applies to all measured grains, reflecting the Imam's role in clarifying jurisprudential extensions of Quranic obligations to the early Muslim community.
